messages:
maria (support): ping — cust reports embedding vector length changed after we pinned a variant yesterday. Their index ingestion now fails with shape mismatch (expected 768, got 1024).

sam (eng): can you paste a failing example?

maria (support): here's the response they pasted. note header X-Embed-Dim: 1024 and array length 1024. they say it worked before pin. cust org id: org-12345.

maria (support): ```
POST /v1/embeddings
Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "model": "redwood-embed-v1",
  "input": "test doc"
}

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
X-Embed-Dim: 1024
{
  "data": [{ "embedding": [0.001, 0.002, /* ... total 1024 floats ... */ ] }]
}
```

sam (eng): weird — did we swap the binary behind the alias? ops-bot showed a pin rollout yesterday: `deploy-bot: rollout complete pin redwood-embed-v1 -> redwood-embed-v1-2026-03-16`

cleo (oncall): checking routing logs for org-12345. requests pinned to alias redwood-embed-v1 were routed to variant id containing `-1024-quant`. I can query alias mapping.

sam (eng): run admin: `rwctl model get-alias redwood-embed-v1` — what does it return?

cleo (oncall): result: `redwood-embed-v1 -> redwood-embed-v1-2026-03-16-1024`

maria (support): customer is asking for immediate rollback or a migration plan. they can't re-index before next week.

sam (eng): options: (A) revert alias to previous 768 build (fast), (B) serve a compatibility shim that downprojects 1024->768 server-side (risky latency/cost), (C) provide a temporary conversion client-side. rollback is simplest.

cleo (oncall): running inventory: `select count(distinct org_id) from routing where alias='redwood-embed-v1' and variant like '%1024%' and timestamp > 1700000000` -> 7 distinct orgs. we need to notify affected customers.

maria (support): i'll draft a rollback notification and ping account teams for the 7 orgs.

sam (eng): initiating alias rollback: `rwctl model set-alias redwood-embed-v1 redwood-embed-v1-2026-03-10-768`

ops-bot: alias-update: redwood-embed-v1 now -> redwood-embed-v1-2026-03-10-768

ops-bot: route-update: traffic for pinned redwood-embed-v1 migrated to 768 variant; draining old 1024 variant

maria (support): telling customer we rolled back alias. ETA ~2 min for their traffic to flip. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

cleo (oncall): verified routing now shows org-12345 traffic hitting redwood-embed-v1-2026-03-10-768.

maria (support): customer confirms embeddings length 768 again and ingestion succeeds.

sam (eng): postmortem action: why did alias point to 1024? suspect automated release job used `:latest` tag during pin and `latest` was updated when we published a 1024 build. I'll open an eng-ml ticket and add a guard that asserts `embed_dim` in model metadata before aliasing.

lee (eng-ml): assigned ENGML-4532. i will add a pre-alias check and a CI test to reject pins where model.metadata.embed_dim differs from alias target expectations.

cleo (oncall): affected orgs: [org-12345, org-67890, org-13579, org-24680, org-11223, org-44556, org-99887]. account teams notified.

sam (eng): follow-ups: (1) ENGML-4532 (guard + CI), (2) ops playbook for dimension mismatch during pin, (3) notify customers and offer assistance re: reindexing if they want to migrate to 1024 in future.

maria (support): cust acknowledged fix and appreciates quick rollback. i'll close support case unless they ask for migration help.

cleo (oncall): note to logs: incident type=embed-dim-mismatch, severity=high, root-cause=alias-published-with-wrong-variant (artifact tagging race).

maria (support): thanks everyone. closing thread.
